title: UniDG: Unified Defect Generation via Defect-Context Editing
claim: Existing generators need per-category adaptation or lack domain priors; a large curated dataset enables one unified foundation model.
layout: Two stacked panels; top four columns left-to-right, bottom dataset pipeline plus donut charts
description: The figure has two stacked parts. Panel (a) is a row of four dash-dotted rounded boxes comparing defect-generation paradigms. They are few-shot generation (SeaS), zero-shot generation (Anomagic), proprietary editing models, and the open-source UniDG foundation model. Each box shows teal input sample boxes, grey diffusion-model blocks, green and blue arrows, flame icons for trainable modules, and output samples. Red crosses and green check marks flag failures and successes, and the last box ends in checks. Panel (b) shows the UDG dataset curation pipeline. An abnormal image and mask pass through an inpainting agent to give a normal image. A captioner agent adds a caption from a JSON template, and a verifier agent filters low-quality pairs. Below the pipeline are donut charts of scenario and defect-category distributions, with a defect-category legend.
caption: Motivation and the proposed UDG dataset. (a) Existing defect-generation paradigms either rely on category-specific few-shot adaptation or on general-purpose image generators that lack defect-specific priors and fine-grained spatial control. (b) The UDG dataset is built by a multi-agent curation pipeline that produces normal-abnormal-mask-caption quadruplets across diverse scenarios and mapped defect categories.
abstract: Generating realistic visual defects is crucial for alleviating the scarcity of abnormal samples in anomaly detection, yet existing methods often rely on category-specific few-shot adaptation and struggle to generalize across objects, defect types, and domains. This limitation stems in part from the lack of paired defect editing data and the fine-grained nature of defect appearance, where subtle variations in scale, texture, and morphology must be preserved while maintaining consistency with the target scene. To address this challenge, we introduce UDG, a dataset of 300K normal-abnormal-mask-caption quadruplets curated from diverse defect-related scenarios, and present UniDG, a unified defect generation model. UniDG formulates defect synthesis as Defect-Context Editing: it extracts reference defect context with adaptive cropping, organizes reference and target inputs in a structured diptych format, and fuses multimodal conditions through MM-DiT attention. We further develop a two-stage training strategy: Diversity-SFT learns diverse transferable defect priors from paired editing data, while optional Consistency-RFT can further improve reference adherence, local realism, and defect-category consistency. Without per-category fine-tuning or using MVTec-AD/VisA for training, UniDG outperforms prior few-shot anomaly generation and image insertion/editing baselines in both synthesis quality and downstream single- and multi-class anomaly detection/localization.
